chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who proposed to a man for his daughter, from a free woman. When it was the night of her entering to her husband, he brought in for her another daughter of his from a slave girl. He said: 'She is returned to her father, and his wife is returned to him, and her dowry is upon her father.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the leper, the blind, the insane, the leper (with skin disease), the harelip, the toothless, the lame, and the bound (in chastity) are returned in case of defect (if not specified).

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ دُخُولِهَا: The night of consummation/entering the marriage
key_terms.مَهِيرَةٍ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father substitutes his slave daughter for his free daughter on the wedding night?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the jurisprudence of 'tadlis' (concealment of defects) in marriage, specifically addressing the scenario where a father substitutes a slave daughter for a free one on the wedding night. It establishes that the original bride is returned to her father, the groom retains the substitute, and the dowry liability falls upon the father, while also listing physical and mental defects that warrant annulment if undisclosed. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and consent in marital contracts, ensuring that hidden defects do not invalidate the union without proper recourse.
